findings.claim: The unit is called Biology Paper 2, but lesson 1 (nervous system half), lesson 4 (DNA, genes and inheritance), lesson 5 (variation and evolution) and lesson 6 (classification and genetic engineering) teach topics 2, 3 and 4, which the spec assigns to Paper 1. Topic 6 (Plant structures and their functions) and topic 8 (Exchange and transport in animals) have no lesson at all.
findings.truth: Spec assessment section: Paper 2 (Biology 2) covers topic 1 plus topics 6, 7, 8 and 9. Topics 2 to 5 are Paper 1. Four of the eight lessons here duplicate lessons that already exist in the sibling unit science-edexcel / biology-paper-1 (its L4 The Nervous System, L5 Genetics and DNA, L6 Evolution and Classification, L7 Genetic Engineering). Missing Paper 2 content: photosynthesis and limiting factors (6.1-6.6), root hair cells, xylem and phloem, transpiration and translocation (6.7-6.13); surface area to volume ratio, alveoli, blood, blood vessels, heart, aerobic and anaerobic respiration and cardiac output (8.1-8.12). Two of the three Paper 2 core practicals are therefore missing too: 6.5 (effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis) and 8.11 (rate of respiration in living organisms). Only 9.5 (quadrats and belt transects) is taught, in lesson 7. Options: (a) build three or four new lessons for topics 6 and 8 and keep the Paper 1 duplicates as revision, (b) build the new lessons and retire the four duplicates, (c) retitle the unit. No lesson text claims 'Paper 2' anywhere, so there is no in-lesson claim to correct. Recommendation: (a) now, decide (b) later.
findings.evidence: spec lines 290-303 and 6316-6322 (Paper 2 content assessed); topic 6 at spec line 1695, topic 8 at line 2007, core practicals 6.5 (line 1726), 8.11 (line 2070), 9.5 (line 2159); sibling brief scripts/_retrofc/units/science-edexcel__biology-paper-1/_brief.json

findings.claim: Lesson 8 teaches trophic levels, pyramids of biomass, the 10% energy transfer figure and why food chains are short, as examined Combined Science content.
findings.truth: The spec lists 9.7 and 9.8 (energy transferred to less useful forms at each trophic level, the shape of a pyramid of biomass; calculating the efficiency of energy transfer between trophic levels) as GCSE in Biology only. They are not in Combined Science. The carbon, water and nitrogen cycle halves of the lesson (9.12-9.15) are correctly in scope. Removing the trophic material would ripple through the lesson title, slug, description, knowledge check 2, flashcards 1-5, practice questions 1 and 3 and the narration, so it is not a surgical fix. Options: mark the section as beyond the spec and keep it as enrichment, or replace it when the topic 6 and 8 lessons in F1 are built. Recommendation: mark as enrichment now.
findings.evidence: spec line 2226 ('Specification points 9.7, 9.8, 9.11, 9.16, 9.17, 9.18 and 9.19 are in the GCSE in Biology only'); specs/edexcel/biology-1BI0.md lines 2387-2410 give 9.7B and 9.8B in full

findings.claim: Lesson 5 teaches speciation and geographic isolation as examined content, defines 'speciation' as a glossary term, tests it in knowledge check 5, and its whole 6-mark extended-response practice question is a speciation question (a volcanic eruption splits an island).
findings.truth: The words 'speciation', 'reproductively isolated' and 'new species' appear nowhere in the Combined Science 1SC0 spec, and nowhere in the separate Biology 1BI0 spec either. Edexcel does not examine speciation at GCSE. The rest of the lesson (Darwin 4.2, antibiotic resistance 4.3, Ardi / Lucy / Leakey 4.4, stone tools 4.5, selective breeding 4.8) is correct and matches the spec word for word, though it is Paper 1 content (see F1). Recommendation: replace the 6-mark question with an evaluate question on selective breeding or genetic engineering (spec 4.14), and keep the speciation paragraphs only if they are marked as enrichment.
findings.evidence: grep of both specs for 'speciation' and 'isolat' returns no biology hit; spec topic 4 at line 1374

findings.claim: The Assisted Reproductive Technology section (IVF and clomifene therapy, narration blocks n16-n20) is wrapped in <div class="higher-only">.
findings.truth: Spec 7.8 ('Explain the use of hormones in Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) including IVF and clomifene therapy') is not a Higher-tier-only statement, so the wrapper hid examinable content from Foundation students. The wrapper on the earlier 'How the Hormones Interact' collapsible is correct, because 7.5 (interactions of oestrogen, progesterone, FSH and LH) is Higher-tier only. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec line 1927 (7.8, Combined Science topic 7). The markdown has lost the bold that marks Higher-tier-only statements, so the tier ruling comes from my knowledge of 1SC0: 7.3, 7.5 and 7.14 are the bold statements in topic 7; 7.6, 7.7 and 7.8 are not.

findings.claim: The whole nitrogen cycle collapsible (nitrogen-fixing, nitrifying and denitrifying bacteria, fertilisers, crop rotation, narration blocks n24-n26) is wrapped in <div class="higher-only">.
findings.truth: Spec 9.15 ('Explain how nitrates are made available for plant uptake, including the use of fertilisers, crop rotation and the role of bacteria in the nitrogen cycle') is not Higher-tier only. The gating was also internally inconsistent: the key fact at n27, practice question 4 and the third conclusion takeaway all cover the same nitrogen material with no gate, so a Foundation student was asked the question but shown no explanation. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec line 2221 (9.15). Bold is lost from the markdown, so the tier ruling comes from my knowledge of 1SC0: topic 9 has no Higher-tier-only statements. The extraction also leaves 9.12-9.15 as clean unbroken blocks, unlike the known-bold 6.4, 6.6, 7.3, 7.5 and 4.11, which are all broken up by stray maths-skill codes.

findings.claim: Higher-tier-only material is gated in the article but its questions are not flagged: practice questions 3 and 4, knowledge checks 2 and 4, and flashcards 9 and 15 all test thyroxine negative feedback or glucagon.
findings.truth: Spec 7.3 (thyroxine and negative feedback) and 7.14 (regulation of blood glucose by glucagon) are Higher-tier only, and the article correctly wraps both in higher-only divs. Six items now carry the '(Higher tier)' prefix. Insulin (7.13), adrenalin (7.2) and BMI (7.17) are both-tier and were left alone.
findings.evidence: spec lines 1877 (7.3) and 1940 (7.14); tier ruling from my knowledge of 1SC0 because the markdown has lost bold

findings.claim: Higher-tier-only material is gated in the article but its questions are not flagged: practice questions 2 and 4, knowledge checks 2, 3 and 4, and flashcards 8-12 all test restriction enzymes, ligase, sticky ends or vectors.
findings.truth: Spec 4.11 (main stages of genetic engineering, including restriction enzymes, ligase, sticky ends and vectors) is Higher-tier only, and the article correctly wraps it. Ten items now carry the '(Higher tier)' prefix. 4.10 (genetic engineering as a process) and 4.14 (evaluate the benefits and risks) are both-tier, so 'What is genetic engineering?', the five-kingdom / three-domain comparison and the evaluate question were left untagged. Note for the orchestrator: the sibling unit science-edexcel / biology-paper-1 tagged its 'Evaluate the use of genetic engineering in agriculture' question and its 'What is genetic engineering?' flashcard as Higher tier. Those two tags look wrong against 4.10 and 4.14 and are worth revisiting.
findings.evidence: spec lines 1428 (4.10), 1433 (4.11) and 1447 (4.14); tier ruling from my knowledge of 1SC0 because the markdown has lost bold

findings.claim: Practice question 6 reads 'Describe the three components of a homeostatic control system', is typed '2 marks - Describe', and its mark scheme lists three credit points then says 'Any two for 2 marks.'
findings.truth: A question that asks for three components with three credit points is a 3-mark question. Typed as 3 marks and the contradictory 'Any two for 2 marks' sentence removed.
findings.evidence: recomputation of the mark scheme against the question stem

findings.claim: Flashcard 2 asks 'Name three conditions regulated by homeostasis.' and answers 'Body temperature / blood glucose / water balance (pick one).'
findings.truth: The answer contradicts the question and is a slash list, which the house flashcard rule forbids. Question changed to ask for one condition and the answer changed to state one condition.
findings.evidence: answer key checked against its own question stem; house flashcard rule (one thing, no list)

findings.claim: Flashcard 13 answers 'Receptor \to sensory neurone \to relay \to motor neurone \to effector.'
findings.truth: Flashcards are a plain-text field, so KaTeX never runs on them and the student sees the literal backslash commands. Replaced with unicode arrows, and 'relay' expanded to 'relay neurone'.
findings.evidence: house convention: *_html fields use entities, plain-text fields use unicode; KaTeX auto-render only fires inside \(...\) or $$...$$ in HTML

findings.claim: Flashcard 9 asks 'Estimated population = (mean count per quadrat \times total area) / ____ area.' and flashcard 14 answers 'Individual \to population \to community \to ecosystem.'
findings.truth: Same raw-LaTeX-in-plain-text fault as F10. Replaced with the unicode multiplication sign and arrows. The quadrat formula itself is correct: estimated population = mean count per quadrat x (total area / quadrat area).
findings.evidence: recomputation of the quadrat estimate formula; house plain-text convention

findings.claim: Practice question 5's fourth mark point reads 'Selective breeding reduces genetic variation in the population / natural selection maintains or increases it (1)'.
findings.truth: Natural selection does not maintain or increase genetic variation; it removes the alleles of the less well suited individuals, so it reduces variation. Mutation is what adds new alleles. The mark point now states only the selective-breeding effect, which is the point the question tests.
findings.evidence: settled fact: natural selection acts on existing variation and removes alleles; mutation is the source of new alleles

findings.claim: Flashcard 11 answers 'Random mutations make some bacteria immune, and antibiotics select for them to reproduce.'
findings.truth: Bacteria become resistant to an antibiotic, not immune. Immunity is a property of a host's immune system. 'Immune' would not be credited on this topic.
findings.evidence: spec 4.3 uses 'resistant organisms' and 'antibiotic resistance in bacteria' (spec line 1384)

findings.claim: Lesson 8 contains the string 'Level 1', 'Level 2', 'Level 3' and 'Level 4' ten times, in the trophic-level definition, the first key fact and the glossary.
findings.truth: The house validator (scripts/_validate_content_json.py) bans the pattern \bLevel\s+[1-9]\b outright as a Level-N band descriptor, and the match is case sensitive. As it stands the validator rejects the whole unit, which would block every edit in this batch. The eight lower-case 'level 2' uses elsewhere in the lesson do not match. Reworded to lower case, which keeps the science and clears the rule.

findings.claim: In lessons 1 and 4, content_html stops in the middle of an open collapsible and the rest of the article is stored in exam_tip_html, together with the stray closing div tags. Lesson 1's article ends at the reflex-arc sequence and its exam-tip box then renders the hot-plate example, a key fact and a whole 'Why Homeostasis Matters' section. Lesson 4's article ends at the Punnett square paragraph and its exam-tip box renders the worked Punnett example, sex determination and whole 'Variation' and 'Human Genome Project' sections.
findings.truth: The two fields were mis-split when the rows were written. The real exam tip is the last paragraph of the run in each case (n21 in lesson 1, n23 in lesson 4). Lessons 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 have the same pattern in milder form: the exam tip paragraph sits at the end of content_html and exam_tip_html is null. Lesson 3 is the only row split correctly. Repairing this means moving two to three kilobytes of HTML between fields and rebalancing the div tags in eight rows, which is a scripted repair rather than a find-and-replace, so it is not in _edits.json.
findings.evidence:
raw dump field lengths: lesson 1 content 6578 / exam_tip 2155, lesson 4 content 7220 / exam_tip 3239; the exam_tip fields open with an article paragraph and contain

headings and unmatched tags

findings.claim: Every lesson's 6-mark extended-response mark scheme uses a 'Mastering (5-6 marks) / Secure (3-4 marks) / Developing (1-2 marks)' ladder.
findings.truth: The house ladder is Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band. 'Mastering / Secure / Developing' is not on the validator's banned list, so nothing fails, but all eight lessons belong on the programme's band-ladder relabel worklist.
findings.evidence: checker brief, house ladder; eight lessons, one 6-mark item each

findings.claim: Lesson 6 is titled 'Natural Selection & Classification' but contains no natural-selection content; it is classification plus genetic engineering. Lesson 8 is titled 'Trophic Levels, Pyramids & the Carbon Cycle' but its description mentions only the carbon, water and nitrogen cycles.
findings.truth: Both descriptions are accurate to the content; the titles are not. Fixing the titles changes slugs and URLs, so it is a decision for the orchestrator, not a surgical edit. Lesson 6's natural-selection material actually sits in lesson 5.
findings.evidence: lesson titles in _brief.json compared with the content_html of lessons 5, 6 and 8

findings.claim: Lesson 8's narration manifest has 28 entries but the lesson carries 32 data-narration-id blocks (n1-n28 in content_html, n30-n33 in conclusion_html).
findings.truth: The four conclusion blocks appear to have no audio. Lessons 5, 6 and 7 all match their manifests exactly, so this is specific to lesson 8. Worth a re-narration check when the F5 and F14 edits are applied and the lesson is re-narrated anyway.
findings.evidence: narration_manifest len 28 in raw/L08.txt; count of data-narration-id attributes across content_html and conclusion_html = 32

summary: The unit's biggest problem is composition, not content: four of eight lessons teach Paper 1 topics that already have lessons in the sibling Paper 1 unit, while topic 6 (plant structures, photosynthesis, transpiration) and topic 8 (exchange and transport, blood, heart, respiration) are missing entirely, along with two of the three Paper 2 core practicals. Within the lessons the science is largely sound; the real errors are tier gating (an ART section and the whole nitrogen cycle wrongly hidden as Higher tier, sixteen Higher-tier-only questions untagged), three answer keys that contradict their own questions, two mark-scheme faults, four flashcards showing raw LaTeX, and ten instances of a string that makes the house validator reject the unit.
